title: Fail closed on unknown Fidelity policy-record keys
objective: Close the source-only policy-record shape gap where otherwise-valid PolicyConfig or PolicyInputs tables may contain misspelled/unknown keys that are silently discarded, including safety-budget override typos and runtime observation/relevance typos, while preserving current Fidelity policy semantics and no-execute validation boundaries.
acceptance: PolicyConfig and PolicyInputs remain metatable-free plain records and validation rejects every unknown key before copying/using config or evaluating runtime policy

an otherwise-valid defaultConfig clone with a misspelled maxRegisteredEntities override fails closed in both FidelityManager.new() and evaluatePolicy() rather than silently retaining the default budget

an otherwise-valid PolicyInputs record with a misspelled visible, directlyObserved, significance, networkRelevance, or entityRelevance signal fails closed instead of silently evaluating the unchanged canonical field
unknown string keys and non-string keys on both policy record types are rejected deterministically without executing caller metamethods or stringifying hostile keys

all 13 currently recognized PolicyConfig keys and all seven currently recognized PolicyInputs keys retain their accepted types/ranges and policy semantics; no field rename, schema-version framework, or new config/input abstraction
retain the project-owned 65,536 registration ceiling and all accepted Fidelity malformed-input, atomicity, determinism, entity-ID, capacity, and state-encapsulation regressions
add deterministic source-only regressions for exact-shape acceptance and config/input extra-key rejection through both pure-policy and manager-step boundaries as applicable
document the closed PolicyConfig and PolicyInputs record boundaries in Docs/FIDELITY_MANAGER.md
canonical CI, live pr-ownership, and fresh independent exact-head review are required before integration
source-only lane: no Roblox Studio, viewport, physical-contact, performance-device, or two-client evidence claim
notes: Capacity-mined against retained Fidelity capacity PR #419 exact head 1f017628bf49365663dfc2db3a30b81ba477a0a3. validateConfig() checks table/metatable and recognized field values but never enumerates keys; copyConfig() then drops extras. The concrete safety case is a cloned default config with typo maxRegsteredEntities = 1: validation accepts the real default maxRegisteredEntities = 4096 and silently ignores the intended override. Follow-up mining found the same closed-record defect in PolicyInputs: validateInputs() checks the seven recognized values but never rejects extra keys, so an input such as directlyObserved=false plus misspelled directlyObseved=true is accepted and silently evaluates false. Fold both defects into one proposed leaf because they share source/tests and validation architecture. This lane is intentionally PROPOSED and sequenced after HG-FIDELITY-MANAGER-STATE-ENCAPSULATION to avoid competing edits in FidelityManager while retained Fidelity lineages remain blocked on trusted-history recovery. Findings: evt-20260812-083100-x9c2p7r4n6-fidelity-config-closed-shape; evt-20260812-083120-w3n8q6v2-fidelity-policyinputs-closed-shape.
